title: Guitar, tenor banjo and bass; leaving banjo for parade trucks
summary: Dawson began guitar around age 30, then banjo and bass, and gave up banjo after rides on parade trucks.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I was going to ask some more about your instrument that you started on. What did you start on? Guitar?
Guitar. Guitar. Yeah. I started on the guitar and after I put the guitar down I picked up tenor banjo.
About how old were you when you started on the guitar?
I was about 30, about 30, 33 something. You didn't start when you were a boy then?
I had a good age when I, and I played the banjo then after the banjo then I'd take no bass violin.
When did you take up the bass do you remember about, was it time of the war or?

Around just about, just about the time of the war. Around 1917, yeah, around, no, around 1912. Before the war. Yeah, before the war I'd take no bass. And from then on I'd play bass, right on. Now and then I'd play, you know, if I catch a job you see, I'd play banjo in between you see, because I never did play study with, you know I'd play study with a band one time and then another fella hired me you know like that. My band wouldn't have enough work all the time to keep me busy. Somebody always wanted a hymn in a different band you see. Well I just kept on playing for the fella who wanted a hymn on the tenor banjo. I had my instrument right there, I'd just pick it up and go and play the job with it you see. But I practically just got so I just put it down all together you see. And sold it, I sold it to Achey. You know a little Achey? Sure. He's the one bought my tenor banjo for me.

I had a good one too. I let him have it. I got tired of being bothered with it, you know. And practically most when I was using it, they would always come from me for congo day to play on them trucks, you know. And I got tired of going on them jobs on it. The weather got so bad and I'd be sitting up on them trucks playing that banjo, I just got tired of doing that and I just put it down. I said I'll get rid of the banjo when the fellas want to hire me. They couldn't get me.
The bass is hard to carry around though too. It has disadvantages too.

Yeah, well, they wasn't using too much bass for the congo parade. Yeah, that's right. Most of the use, you know, plenty, they'd like, the instrumentation they were practically using would be drum, tenor, banjo, cornet, trombone, something like that, clarinet. And they'd be satisfied. Five, four, five pieces like that, they'd be satisfied, you see. The bass was so awkward to be carrying on them trucks. You had to get them trucks high, you got to be carrying it up and down on them trucks. So, it was too inconvenient. Then the weather got, come as it's getting bad and getting so cold and you'd have to be clocking up with coats and things on. You couldn't be too stuffed up to be playing in. Half of the time, you'd have to stand up to play the bass, you see. Sure. And them trucks, they want you to be playing while the trucks is going, you see. Long time ago, they wouldn't, they didn't want that. They'd let you wait until they make a stop.
